Summary of the degradation pathways related to the organic cations in a perovskite solar cell and mechanisms of BOP-Cl on stabilizing organic cations in a perovskite solar cell device. Most state-of-the-art PSCs utilize a formamidinium (FA) based A site lead halide composition. However, ion migration and ionic loss of the organic cation trigger various degradation pathways. Within the bulk perovskite, hydrogen bonding between the halide and the proton of the ammonium ion in FA plays an important role in stabilizing crystal phases. However, the strength of these interactions could be significantly varied at the surfaces depending on different terminations of the crystal structure, leading to much more pronounced ion migrations at the surface and grain boundary of the devices. Furthermore, the presence of an unprotected proton on the ammonium group can adversely affect the chemical and phase stability of the perovskite layer due to its acidity. In a PSC device, extrinsic reactions can happen at the interface between the metal oxide charge transport layer and perovskites, leading to the deprotonation of ammonium groups to volatile amines and the subsequent formation of lead iodides. Phosphine oxide derivatives are widely used in perovskite LEDs because oxygen can donate electron density to the exposed Pb2+ ions and passivate surface non-radiative recombination pathways. Similarly, the electron-rich oxygen can also form hydrogen bonds with protons in the ammonium group of FA, which is often understated. Our previous work utilized triphenylphosphine oxide in the device because of its benefits in reducing metastable behavior (e.g. initial burn-in at timescale of minutes to hours) and improving the long-term stability of the solar cell. Because cation migration can cause an initial burn-in of the device under reverse bias (i.e. at flat band condition), we therefore pivot to believe that interactions between the phosphine oxide and the organic cations (and not the exposed Pb2+ ions) are the dominating cause of this improvement in a solar cell device.
